question: Why do we even need health care economics in our hospitals?

options.B: Medical treatments always cost the same
options.C: Patients demand too many free services
options.D: Resources like money and staff are limited

explanation: Spot on! Economics is simply about how we handle scarcity—meaning our money, time, and staff are limited, but patient needs are endless. You've got this! [learn more](GST322_U5_T1#GST322_U5_T1_h1)

question: How does health care economics actually affect you as a nurse on the ward?

options.A: It removes all financial stress from the hospital
options.B: It stops nurses from ever using advanced equipment
options.C: It dictates how staff manage limited supplies and time
options.D: It determines the exact salary of every patient

explanation: Exactly! Every day on the ward, you live economics when juggling limited shifts, gloves, and medication supplies to give the best care possible. [learn more](GST322_U5_T1#GST322_U5_T1_h1)

question: What is the name of the economic indicator used to measure a country's total output of goods and services?
explanation: Great job! Gross domestic product (GDP) is just the big financial scorecard showing how healthy a nation's overall economy is. [learn more](GST322_U5_T1#GST322_U5_T1_h2)

question: What usually happens to public health funding when the national economy goes through a tough patch?

options.A: Private clinics take over all public patients
options.B: Hospitals receive a sudden surge of extra grants
options.C: The cost of medical care drops to zero everywhere
options.D: Government health budgets are often reduced

explanation: Spot on. When money is tight nationally, governments collect less revenue and unfortunately tend to slash public sector budgets, including healthcare. [learn more](GST322_U5_T1#GST322_U5_T1_h2)

question: Which expense usually takes up the biggest slice of a hospital's budget?
explanation: Correct! Paying the dedicated nurses, doctors, and support staff who keep the hospital running takes up the largest share of operating costs. [learn more](GST322_U5_T1#GST322_U5_T1_h3)

question: When local nurses aren't paid well and move abroad for better opportunities, what is this workforce loss called?
explanation: Well done! 'Brain drain' describes when skilled professionals leave their home country seeking greener pastures, which really hits our local health sector hard. [learn more](GST322_U5_T1#GST322_U5_T1_h3)

question: What often happens when patients simply cannot afford the high cost of their prescribed medications?

options.A: Pharmacies are forced to give all drugs away
options.B: They may skip doses or stop taking them
options.C: Hospital admissions instantly drop to zero
options.D: They automatically receive free government refills

explanation: Exactly. When out-of-pocket costs are too high, patients often try to stretch their drugs by skipping doses, which delays their healing. [learn more](GST322_U5_T1#GST322_U5_T1_h4)

question: Why does a drop in local currency value make medications so much more expensive?

options.A: Doctors start prescribing more expensive brands
options.B: Governments place heavy taxes on local pharmacies
options.C: Many essential drugs and raw materials are imported
options.D: Local factories stop producing tablets entirely

explanation: Spot on! Because we import a lot of our medicines and raw ingredients, a weaker currency means it costs much more to bring them into the country. [learn more](GST322_U5_T1#GST322_U5_T1_h4)

question: In a healthcare setting, what does 'resource allocation' mean?

options.A: Calculating the exact profit made by a pharmacy
options.B: The process of admitting patients to private rooms
options.C: Writing new nursing textbooks for students
options.D: How funds, staff, and supplies are distributed

explanation: Great! Resource allocation is simply deciding how to share out available money, materials, and staff to where they are needed most. [learn more](GST322_U5_T1#GST322_U5_T1_h5)

question: Why is it important for nurse managers to keep a close eye on ward inventory and supplies?

options.A: To ensure patients never pay for their medications
options.B: To calculate the daily income of every doctor
options.C: To prevent waste, expiration, and supply shortages
options.D: To increase the workload of junior nursing staff

explanation: Correct! Good inventory checks stop supplies from expiring on the shelf and ensure the ward never runs out during an emergency. [learn more](GST322_U5_T1#GST322_U5_T1_h5)

question: What does an 'out-of-pocket' payment system mean for a patient?

options.A: Patients pay directly for medical services themselves
options.B: The government covers all medical bills automatically
options.C: Health insurance pays every cent of hospital costs
options.D: Services are provided entirely free of charge

explanation: Spot on! Out-of-pocket means the patient pays cash right there at the point of care out of their own wallet. [learn more](GST322_U5_T1#GST322_U5_T1_h6)

question: How do upfront hospital user fees usually affect patients with little income?

options.A: They are given free medications upon arrival
options.B: They are automatically transferred to private suites
options.C: They receive faster treatment than wealthy patients
options.D: They delay seeking care until their condition worsens

explanation: Exactly right. Worrying about money often causes vulnerable patients to stay home until a simple illness turns into a major emergency. [learn more](GST322_U5_T1#GST322_U5_T1_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT a smart way to make healthcare more cost-effective?

options.A: Investing heavily in community preventive care
options.C: Promoting the use of safe generic drugs
options.D: Shifting routine tasks to trained support cadres

explanation: Well done! Buying only pricey brand-name drugs wastes money when safe, affordable generic options work just as well. [learn more](GST322_U5_T1#GST322_U5_T1_h7)

question: A clinic trains community health workers to give routine vaccines so nurses can focus on complex cases. What is this strategy called?
explanation: Spot on! 'Task shifting' safely passes appropriate duties to trained support staff, helping the healthcare team work smarter and save costs. [learn more](GST322_U5_T1#GST322_U5_T1_h7)
